title: Can Formal Invariants Detect Prompt Injection Before It Affects Output?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Bridges formal alignment theory directly to a concrete, immediate safety threat (prompt injection). If formal behavioral contracts can serve as early-warning systems, this provides a practical defense with theoretical grounding. Highly actionable.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Prompt injection attacks are well-documented and easy to craft. Running an instruction-tuned model and measuring output changes, activation deviations, and schema violations uses standard tools. Beginners can execute this with a pre-trained model and basic activation extraction.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three detection methods (output change, activation anomaly, schema violation) applied to a set of injection attacks. Each method is relatively simple, but comparing three approaches adds breadth. Could be narrowed to two methods for tighter scope.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
